title: JRE 2273 - Adam Curry
guestBio: Adam Curry is an internet entrepreneur, former MTV VJ, and podcasting pioneer. He is the co-host, along with John C. Dvorak, of the "No Agenda" podcast.
tldr: Adam Curry discusses his background as an MTV VJ and his transition into internet entrepreneurship and podcasting
Conversation covers the history and evolution of podcasting, with Curry's role as a pioneer in the medium
Discussion of the No Agenda podcast with John C. Dvorak and their approach to media criticism
Topics around internet culture, media manipulation, and independent content creation
Adam shares insights on building an audience and the business side of podcasting
Joe and Adam explore themes of digital independence and alternative media
recap:
Joe Rogan sits down with Adam Curry, the former MTV VJ turned internet pioneer who helped shape the podcasting landscape we know today. Curry brings his unique perspective on how he transitioned from mainstream television to building a career in the early days of the internet, where few understood the potential of what was coming.

The conversation dives deep into Curry's role as a podcasting pioneer and his ongoing work with the No Agenda podcast alongside John C. Dvorak. Throughout the episode, Adam discusses how he saw opportunities in digital media before most people were paying attention, and how he's built a loyal following through independent content creation. He shares stories about the early internet days and how the landscape has changed dramatically.

One of the central themes is the power of independent media and how creators can build audiences without relying on traditional gatekeepers. Adam talks about the challenges and rewards of running a podcast that doesn't follow mainstream narratives, and how his audience has grown over the years through word of mouth and genuine engagement.

The discussion touches on how the internet has democratized content creation and given people the tools to build their own platforms. Curry emphasizes the importance of maintaining independence and not being beholden to corporate interests or advertising pressure that might compromise editorial integrity.

Throughout the conversation, Joe and Adam explore the broader implications of alternative media, the role of podcasting in the current media landscape, and how audiences are increasingly turning to independent creators for news and analysis they feel they can trust more than mainstream outlets.
